title: Axis Mundi, Mountain, Tree, Pillar, Shadow & Wetland Context Atlas
kind: comparative religion + analytical psychology + ecology boundary atlas
purpose: Use external scholarship to sharpen Mountain/Tree/Pillar/Axis, Shadow and Swamp without collapsing comparative symbols or turning literal ecosystems into moral metaphors.
epistemic_rule: External traditions and sciences retain their own meanings. Potatoverse use is structural comparison unless independently evidenced.

axis_mundi.finding: Religion scholarship uses axis mundi for a world-center/connective image that can appear as cosmic mountain, world tree, pillar, ladder, temple/city and related forms connecting heaven, earth and underworld.
axis_mundi.structural_use: This supports treating Mountain, Tree, Pillar and Ladder as alternate representations of vertical connection rather than forcing them into one literal stack.
axis_mundi.boundary: A shared axis function does not imply historical identity between traditions.

mountain.finding: Sacred mountains can function as centers/orienters joining heaven and earth, but traditions assign very different meanings and shapes to them.
mountain.project_use: Mountain is best defined by integration/orientation/perspective and circulation, not by generic holiness or domination.

cave.finding: Comparative religion sources frequently treat caves as womb/death/emergence passages and sometimes as centers/axis openings connecting regions; mountain and cave imagery can be combined.
cave.project_use: Cave is a useful secondary comparator for inward descent, burial and re-emergence around Door/Below, but should remain a room-detail node rather than a new primary floor.

shadow.finding: In Jungian analytical psychology, shadow refers to elements not integrated into conscious personality. These may include aggression/envy but also vulnerable, loving, realistic or creative capacities that were denied or undeveloped.
shadow.project_use: Project Shadow should be a crosscutting occlusion/integration layer, not a synonym for evil, Below, demon or Swamp.
shadow.caution: Do not use a Jungian concept as a diagnosis of named people or groups.

literal_wetland.finding: Wetlands, including swamps, are transition zones shaped by hydrology, soils and adapted vegetation; they can support important ecological processes and are not inherently degraded systems.
literal_wetland.project_use: The Potatoverse Swamp must remain explicitly project-symbolic. Its negative system-state meaning must not be projected onto literal swamps/wetlands.
literal_wetland.useful_analogy: The ecological idea of a transition zone is useful only cautiously: saturation changes what can live and how material cycles, but real wetland ecology is not a model of moral failure.

resulting_project_rules: Mountain, Tree, Pillar and Ladder may overlap as connective-function projections without becoming synonyms.
Shadow is crosscutting and can exist in proclaimed Heaven-facing ideals, ordinary World behavior or buried Below material.
Swamp is a project symbolic attractor/system-state; literal wetlands remain ecologically distinct.
Cave may be used as a secondary Door/Below comparator for inward passage, burial and emergence, but should not become another mandatory floor.
The project should classify function before moral valence.
